plainLanguage: Kanuni ya msingi ni kwamba intoxication yenyewe si defence kwa criminal charge. Section 14 ina exceptions na matumizi maalum: defence inaweza kutokea chini ya subsection (2) ikiwa intoxication ilimfanya accused asielewe anachofanya na pia ikatokana bila consent yake na malicious/negligent act ya mwingine, au intoxication ikamfanya insane. Subsection (4) pia inaruhusu intoxication kuzingatiwa wakati wa kuamua kama required intention iliundwa.
meaning: Section 14 ina routes tofauti ambazo hazipaswi kuchanganywa. (1) inaanza na general exclusion. (2) ina defence yenye conjunctive requirements. (3) inaeleza legal consequence baada ya subsection (2) defence kuthibitishwa: paragraph (a) leads to discharge; paragraph (b) invokes Penal Code na Criminal Procedure Act provisions on insanity. (4) ni inquiry tofauti kuhusu formation of intention required by an offence. (5) inaweka narcotics/drugs ndani ya maana ya intoxication.
keyPoints: (2): Accused lazima, by reason of intoxication, not understand what he was doing, pamoja na (a) involuntary intoxication caused by another's malicious/negligent act au (b) insanity by reason of intoxication.
(3): Consequence ya (2)(a) ni discharge; kwa (2)(b), insanity provisions za Penal Code na Criminal Procedure Act apply.
(4): Intoxication inaweza kuzingatiwa katika kuamua kama accused formed intention, specific or otherwise, ambayo bila hiyo asingekuwa guilty.
(5): Intoxication includes state produced by narcotics or drugs.

legalTerms.meaning: Kwa section 14, inajumuisha pia state produced by narcotics or drugs.
Sharti la subsection (2)(a) linalotofautisha intoxication iliyosababishwa bila consent ya accused.
Intention ambayo inaweza kuwa necessary kwa offence husika na ambayo formation yake inaweza kuchunguzwa chini ya subsection (4).
Matokeo yaliyotajwa na subsection (3) kwa defence inayofanikiwa chini ya subsection (2)(a).

examples.title: Kunyweshwa bila kujua
examples.scenario: Mtu anawekewa intoxicating substance bila consent yake na hali hiyo inamfanya asielewe anachofanya.
examples.analysis: Facts zinaweza kuleta subsection (2)(a), lakini lazima requirements zake zote zithibitishwe; si kila involuntary consumption automatically determines the case.

examples.title: Voluntary drinking na required intention
examples.scenario: Accused alikunywa kwa hiari na anashtakiwa offence ambayo guilt inategemea formation ya particular intention.
examples.analysis: General defence ya subsection (2)(a) haitokani tu na voluntary intoxication, lakini subsection (4) inaweza kufanya intoxication relevant kwa swali kama required intention iliundwa.

cases.name: Adam Salehe @ Ramadhani v Republic
cases.relevance: The Court considered whether intoxication could stand as a defence to murder and restated the limited statutory circumstances under section 14.

cases.name: Republic v Abdalah Salim @ Swaha
cases.relevance: The High Court applied section 14 to an accused who relied on drunkenness and emphasized that intoxication is generally not a defence except within the statutory conditions.

cases.name: Republic v Mbavumbili
cases.relevance: The Court discussed section 14(4), focusing on whether intoxication affected formation of the intention required for the offence.

history.summary: Section 14 has long distinguished intoxication as a defence from intoxication as evidence relevant to intention. The current R.E. 2022 official text contains subsections (1)-(5).
notes: During digitisation, subsection (3) was found missing from the repository copy and has now been restored verbatim from the official R.E. 2022 source.
The statutory cross-reference in subsection (3) is to insanity provisions of the Penal Code and Criminal Procedure Act.

expertPerspectives.label: Mtazamo A
expertPerspectives.view: A rigorous analysis checks both inability to understand and one of the two statutory causes/conditions in paragraphs (a) or (b). Mere drunkenness is not enough.

expertPerspectives.label: Mtazamo B
expertPerspectives.view: Even where subsection (2) defence fails, intoxication may remain evidentially relevant if the offence requires an intention without which guilt would not arise.

expertPerspectives.label: Mtazamo C
expertPerspectives.view: How intoxication arose is crucial for subsection (2)(a), while subsection (4) asks a different question about actual formation of intention.

debateQuestion: Je, accused anategemea full defence ya subsection (2), insanity route, au anatumia intoxication chini ya subsection (4) kupinga formation ya required intention?
disclaimer: Ufafanuzi huu si maandishi rasmi ya sheria.
